claims.text: A tailored aging treatment can induce stepwise, controllable coherent nanoprecipitation in a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
SCCP induced by aging will improve helium-irradiation tolerance in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
SCCP can preserve mechanical integrity by providing high strength together with tensile ductility in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Introducing SCCP through aging will not compromise processing practicality.
The aging treatment will produce coherent nanoprecipitates uniformly dispersed throughout the matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient radiation-defect and helium sinks.
The nanoprecipitates impede helium-bubble coalescence.
The nanoprecipitates suppress helium-bubble growth.
Coherent SCCP interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent SCCP interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could initiate premature cracking.
The combination of helium trapping and stress relief will mitigate irradiation-induced damage.
The aged alloy will have smaller helium bubbles than the unaged alloy after identical irradiation.
The aged alloy will have a more uniform helium-bubble distribution than the unaged alloy.
The aged alloy will exhibit a higher helium-bubble number density, indicative of suppressed bubble growth.
After irradiation, the aged alloy will retain yield strength within approximately a 10–15% reduction.
The unaged tungsten-based refractory HEA will show larger helium bubbles than the SCCP-treated alloy.
The unaged alloy will exhibit more pronounced irradiation hardening or embrittlement than the SCCP-treated alloy.
Approximately 200 keV helium irradiation at about 900 °C represents reactor-relevant plasma-facing conditions.
Radiation-tolerance benefits depend on obtaining a homogeneous and controllable precipitate distribution.
Prior SCCP evidence establishes enhanced strength and ductility but does not establish its quantitative effect on helium-bubble suppression.
